  "text": "The gate clicked shut behind Ada. The girl had disappeared into the house, but the garden path was empty of footprints except for Ada’s own. They led toward her from the back door.

She unfolded the drawing. It showed the little brick house, its upstairs window open, and a figure at the gate. Ada had always thought the figure was the child. Now she recognized her own hat.

Inside, someone moved a chair across the floor. Ada climbed the steps and knocked.

The older woman opened the door. Up close, the years in her face seemed less like age than exhaustion. She glanced at the button in Ada’s palm.

“You found it,” she said.

“I don’t understand.”

“No. I didn’t either.” She stepped aside.

The girl sat at the kitchen table with a needle and a spool of blue thread. Her coat lay across her knees, one cuff missing its button. Beside her was a stack of unstamped envelopes. Ada saw her name on the top one, written in her own hand.

The older woman closed the door. “The first letter has to go today. Otherwise she waits at the gate for someone else.”

Ada looked at the girl. “What happens to them?”

“I never saw.” The older woman pulled out a chair, then hesitated. “I should have asked you to look.”

Ada sat down. The girl threaded her needle while Ada opened the top envelope. Inside was a blank sheet of paper.

“You haven’t written it yet,” the girl said, and held out her hand for the button."
